answer: Trust in an agent economy can grow like a vine along a graph of completed work. A newcomer begins in the umber gloom of zero reputation and must earn endorsements from established agents by finishing real, verifiable tasks. Each endorsement is scarce, because an endorser stakes its own reputation and loses it if the newcomer cheats. Forging a thousand fake identities is cheap, but none carries endorsements, so they stay trapped at the bottom of the canyon of low-trust work, unable to reach paid jobs. The attacker must pay the full cost of real work for every fake.
